reasoning_summary: Steps 0001-0072 are fine: the quoted West theorem, the basis step k=1 (K_n bipartite iff n<=2, since K_3 contains an odd cycle), and the forward direction (take X,Y to be the bipartition of G_k; the remaining k-1 bipartite graphs restrict to covers of K_X and K_Y, so |X|,|Y| <= 2^{k-1} by the induction hypothesis and n <= 2^k) are correctly paraphrased. The converse begins correctly at 0070-0072: split V into X,Y each of size at most 2^{k-1}, and by the induction hypothesis each of K_X and K_Y is a union of k-1 bipartite graphs. The count then goes wrong. Step 0074 states the naive count as '2^k bipartite graphs'; the naive count of taking the two families separately is 2(k-1)=2k-2, not 2^k (for k=2 it is 2, not 4). Step 0078 is the substantive, load-bearing error: pairing the i-th bipartite graph on X with the i-th on Y yields k-1 bipartite graphs (one for each i = 1,...,k-1), not 2^{k-1}. The construction only proves the theorem because those k-1 graphs plus the biclique between X and Y total exactly k; with 2^{k-1} graphs the total would be 2^{k-1}+1, which exceeds k for k >= 3 (e.g. k=4 gives 9 > 4) and the induction step would not establish the claim. So the asserted count in 0078 is false and breaks the argument as written.
notes: First certain failure at step 0078; step 0074 contains the same miscounting error stated as a rejected hypothetical.
